# Reordering sparse updates before relative compression

Test whether a decoder that knows the old catalogue and already reconstructed fields can use that context for both the change mask and field values. The receiver projects the old schema onto the encoded new schema, initializes absent fields to empty strings, then processes columns in publication order. An outer XZ stream covers every tag, payload and schema change. Keys for new and removed records are transmitted. Evaluate exact reconstruction of both already-used Tate development intervals against every earlier comparator and against an equally searched own-field codec. Require at least 5% fewer total bytes in each comparison on each interval. Restrict development and decision making to Tate.

Encode each column's changed key set by sorted rank gaps. Test identifier order, old own-value order, or other old-field orders; the full codec can also transmit a symmetric difference from an earlier field's mask. For the values evaluate XZ-compressible literals, byte delta instructions against the concatenated old values, and instructions relative to an old-column dictionary. Supply same-row previous-field values and anchored single-span replacements learned from already reconstructed fields as additional dictionary candidates in the contextual method. The own-field control gets the same byte encoder, choice of dictionary or aligned source, delta options and outer compressor, using old own-field values and key/own-value sorts only. Advertise each selected order, mask and dictionary. Candidate generation and local compressed-size selection are part of the encoder. Wire size is the sole performance endpoint. The independent implementation must decode from the base and wire. Check changed schema and supplementary Unicode against a synthetic example.
